content: One never notices what has been done; one can only see what remains to be done.
author: Marie Curie
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

Marie Curie understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: What would change in your daily outlook if you truly lived by this perspective?
